analysis:
Only docs/architecture/inference.md changed. The patch adds a section (head lines ~3541-3575) describing cluster service listeners: they restart when the cable port or address changes, when the pairing changes, or stop when no pairing exists, rechecked at most every 5 s. A pairing store that cannot be read leaves the listener unchanged. The supplied units are base lines 5337-5432 and head lines 1-419. Those ranges do not include the added section (head 3541-3575), and the patch excerpt is truncated. The added text itself was only seen in the truncated excerpt. The supplied excerpts are unchanged surrounding documentation: Qwen TP assistant, planned stop ordering, batch and rank ledger text.

No source code, control or configuration changes are visible, so no concrete security regression can be shown. The documented behavior is consistent with the threat model. A listener keyed to a pairing refuses handshakes from a later pairing, and the edge secret is never compared. The control node is dropped when the pairing names another member. The documented design leaves the control lease listener restarts and stops without a log line. That is an observability gap only, not a vulnerability. Documentation drift does not affect TB-002, TB-011 or the cache threat T-041.

Remaining integration questions: the code in ClusterService.swift (listenerChange, ensureResponder) and ClusterSetupLinkExchange was not supplied. Whether it matches this documentation, and whether listener restarts preserve handshake rejection for stale pairings, is unverified. The truncated patch tail was not seen.
